newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech central bank calls news conference for Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Czech central bank calls news conference for Thurs.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Wednesday that Governor Josef Tosovsky and executive director Jiri Pospisil would discuss the central bank's 1997 monetary policy outlook with journalists on Thursday.
Spokesman Martin Svehla said in a statement that the news conference will begin at 10 a.m. local time (0900 GMT).

Last week, the CNB announced targets for 1997 M2 growth between 8 and 12 percent. The central bank also said it aimed for year-on-year inflation at the end of 1997 to dip below eight percent if the government met its price deregulation targets.
The central bank said the "main risk for the coming period" was wage growth outpacing industrial output increases.
Year-on-year 1996 inflation was 8.6 percent. In the CNB's latest official statistics, year-on-year M2 growth was 9.8 percent at the end of October, slowing from 22.4 percent a year ago.

The CNB tigtened monetary policy in late June, raising its discount rate one full percentage point to 10.5 percent and increasing minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent of deposits.
